question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer must implement an Application Performance Monitoring (APM) for the production servers on the Cisco Nexus 93180 Series Switch-based infrastructure in datacenter 1. The APM solution must meet these requirements: it must copy all inbound and outbound production traffic; and it must support real-time telemetry. Which configuration must be used on datacenter 1 switches to meet these objectives?
context: Topology: two data centers, each with a pair of spine switches connecting to three leaf switches, connecting to production/APM servers across VLANs 3018, 2408, 1812.
imageNote: Diagram: a Layer 3 Network connects DC1 (N9K-DC-1-Spine-1/2, Leaf1-3, hosting PROD-SVR-1 on VLAN3018 and PROD-SVR-2 on VLAN2408) to DC2 (N9K-DC-2-Spine-1/2, Leaf1-3, hosting APM-SVR-1 on VLAN1810).
options:
monitor session 1 source ip 172.30.18.12,172.24.8.39
monitor session 1 destination ip 172.18.10.1
monitor session 1 type rspan
monitor session 1 filter vlan 3018,2408

monitor session 1 type erspan-source
source vlan 3018,2408 both
vrf default
destination ip 172.18.10.1
erspan-id 19
no shut

monitor session 1 type rspan-source
source vlan 3018,2408 both
vrf management
destination vlan 2810
span-id 19
no shut

monitor session 1 source vlan 3018,2408
monitor session 1 type IP
monitor session 1 destination ip 172.18.10.1
no monitor session 1 shutdown
theory: Copying both inbound and outbound production traffic across VLANs, and delivering it off-box to a remote APM collector while still supporting the switch's own real-time telemetry, calls for an ERSPAN source session, which unlike SPAN or RSPAN is IP-routable and doesn't consume a local monitoring port, with sources specified as both direction so ingress and egress traffic on the relevant VLANs are captured and sent to the collector's IP with a unique erspan-id and the appropriate VRF for reachability. RSPAN and simple VLAN-based SPAN configurations shown in the other options can't route the mirrored copy to a remote analyzer the way ERSPAN's IP-based destination can. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — ERSPAN Source Sessions for Bidirectional Production Traffic Capture)
